learn.heading: Field lessons
learn.archive-note: Discovered explanations stay here. New lessons follow your actions and finds. You can reread them at any time.
learn.tip.welcome: Start with Gunther at the museum.
learn.text.welcome:
Pieces of old objects lie beneath the valley. You will locate them with an instrument, dig them up with a hoe, and restore whole objects from fragments.

First visit the museum and speak to Gunther at the counter. He provides a book and a field surveyor for free. Bring your own hoe: the basic one works.

Open the book as an item or press {{journal}}. It remembers sites, fragments, and your next step.
learn.tip.search: At a site, hold the surveyor and press the action button.
learn.text.search:
Open My Journey and select a dig objective. It lists the location and remaining time. Travel to that map; you do not need to guess the exact tile.

Select the field surveyor in your backpack and press the usual action button, the one used to talk to villagers. It will signal the nearest available find.

The surveyor locates traces. Your hoe digs them up. The book keeps records and restores objects.
learn.tip.signal: Follow the arrow until a golden frame appears on the ground.
learn.text.signal:
The arrow above your character shows the route to a find. It points toward the next turn on dry land: take paths around water and rocks. Its color and the instrument message help you judge the distance.

Move closer. A golden frame appears automatically, marking the exact tile for your hoe. If the arrow fades before a frame appears, use the surveyor again.

An arrow alone is not an exact digging spot. Keep approaching instead of digging at random.
learn.tip.dig: Switch to your hoe and strike inside the golden frame.
learn.text.dig:
The golden frame marks a real find. Switch from the surveyor to your hoe and till the ground inside it with a normal tool strike.

The mark stays when you put the surveyor away. Any hoe works; a charged strike from an upgraded hoe also counts marked tiles.

A flash, floating fragments, and an updated site counter confirm collection. Hold the surveyor again to search for the next find.
learn.tip.fragments: Fragments stay in the book and combine into whole objects.
learn.text.fragments:
Excavations yield fragments: pieces of ancient objects. They go straight into your book and take no backpack slots. The message after a find shows your balance and the current project cost.

Each research field has its own fragments. Valley pieces pay for valley projects; coastal pieces pay for coastal projects.

Open Finds, select the current project, and check the counter. Keep digging if you need more. Ordinary worm spots can also yield fragments when that option is enabled in Settings.
learn.tip.keystones: One part replaces up to 12 fragments when restoring an object.
learn.text.keystones:
A keystone is an extra restoration material. It stays in the book and belongs to its research field.

Enable a part on the current project page to lower the cost by 12 fragments, to a minimum of one. It is consumed only when restoration succeeds. Using one is optional.

Finishing every find at a site guarantees a part. Parts may also appear during excavation or as rewards for donating an object to Gunther for the first time.
learn.tip.restore: Open the current project in Finds and choose Restore.
learn.text.restore:
When you have enough fragments, the journal adds a restoration task to My Journey. Open it or find your current project in Finds.

The project page shows your supply and the cost. Press Restore: materials are spent and a real object enters your backpack. It needs a free slot. You can restore objects in any location.

Discuss the first cup with Gunther at the museum so he can help read its story. In later projects, an ancient part may replace some fragments; its use is always shown in the price.
learn.tip.relics: The whole object is in your backpack: read its properties in Finds.
learn.text.relics:
A restored object is a real backpack item. Open its page in Finds to read its history, purpose, and any special effect or cooldown.

Hold an active relic and press the action button to use it. Lamps can be placed. Every object has its own conditions, explained in its description.

You can donate the first copy through its page while at the museum. Gunther takes the backpack item and rewards you with gold and a keystone. Donation is optional; you can keep the object.
learn.tip.chapters: New research fields and stories appear in Research after discoveries.
learn.text.chapters:
Archaeology begins with one story. Gunther connects the first cup's mark with the old mountain workshops. Later, restored objects provide clues for conversations about other places.

Open Research → Where Finds Lead when that entry appears. It records the source of your clue and your next conversation partner. Available transport alone does not open a new region's field notes.

My Journey gathers available actions. Choose a task, read its details and pin it on screen if you wish. You do not need to pursue every story at once.
learn.tip.weather: A weather clue appeared: check its deadline in Research.
learn.text.weather:
Observed rain or a storm may expose a special site. Its location and deadline appear in the weather chapter and My Journey.

Use the familiar tools: surveyor, then hoe on the marked tile. Collect every find to earn the completion reward. Finishing each type for the first time unlocks a special relic; collect it with the button on the chapter page.

The site has a deadline. A reward you have already earned waits in the book indefinitely.
learn.tip.nature: An unusual event has left an excavation clue.
learn.text.nature:
Snow, a new season, and a new meteorite can leave unusual traces. Open the natural events chapter in Research to learn what happened, where to search, and how much time remains.

Use the surveyor and hoe as at a normal site. Finish every find for an extra reward. Collect the ready relic on its story page; it can wait until you have backpack room.
learn.tip.workshop: The blueprint begins the workshop story.
learn.text.workshop:
You discovered a mechanism blueprint among the fragments. This is a story find: the plan and later components are recorded in the book, not stored in your backpack.

Open the blueprint chapter in Research. At the museum, use the study button on the blueprint page. Then find the named craftsperson, stand nearby, and use the conversation button on that page. Components begin appearing at digs after the required conversation.

The story page shows the next step and missing materials. You cannot assemble the mechanism before completing those steps.
learn.tip.residents: Someone may recognize a restored object.
learn.text.residents:
Some ordinary objects remind villagers of the past. The resident stories chapter names the person involved in your new clue.

Stand near them, open that story page in the book, and choose its conversation button. This may open a separate dig. Search with your usual tools, return after finishing, and speak through the story page again. Collect the keepsake reward in the book.

My Journey reminds you which step comes next.
learn.tip.shipwreck: Coastal discoveries opened a separate story in Research.
learn.text.shipwreck:
This sea clue has its own sequence of actions. Open its page in Research and read the current step: sometimes you need the right conditions, sometimes an excavation.

Your regular surveyor and hoe work here too. Story finds and progress stay in the book. If there is nothing to dig yet, follow the next-step description and its objective in My Journey.
learn.tip.gallery: Collections and rewards are now available in My Study.
learn.text.gallery:
Restored objects form themed collections. My Study shows discovered sets, reward requirements, and where to collect a reward.

Your restoration record stays even after donating an object. A home display needs physical objects and a display case: place items from your backpack and retrieve them later.

A collection record remembers your discovery. The actual exhibit decorates your home.
learn.tip.museum: Gunther has new activities in the museum archive.
learn.text.museum:
The museum chapter now offers orders, duplicate exchanges, and exhibitions. Choose one task to start; its page explains the requirements and reward.

Donations require real backpack items and a museum visit. Simply reading a page spends nothing. Exhibitions use objects in your own display case; read the conditions before starting.

Ready rewards and current requests also appear in My Journey.
learn.tip.mastery: Excavation experience brings you closer to a specialty choice.
learn.text.mastery:
Digs and completed stories grant archaeology experience. Your current level appears below the book title.

At levels 5 and 10, choose a permanent bonus in the mastery chapter. Compare the descriptions: they help different activities, while every find and story remains available with any choice.

Gunther can also upgrade your surveyor. Equipment lists the required level, materials, and price.
learn.tip.frontiers: Your notes now include distant research routes.
learn.text.frontiers:
Distant field notes follow a particular find and conversation. You also need transport to reach the region. Where Finds Lead keeps the reason each route opened.

Use your familiar surveyor and hoe there. Each new field has its own fragments and current project. Future objects are not listed ahead of discovery.

Open routes stay available. Continue with one story that suits you; you do not need to explore every region at once.
learn.tip.expeditions: Familiar stories have led to a riddle expedition.
learn.text.expeditions:
This expedition involves more than digging. Stand near the named villager and use the conversation button on the expedition page. Read the clue to choose the research location.

Locate finds with the surveyor and excavate with your hoe. Later you will discuss the evidence and assemble an object. Reread conversations or reveal hints on the expedition page.

An incorrect answer lets you continue examining the puzzle. Return to the evidence and try again.

journal.title: Archaeology · Secrets of the Valley
journal.guide:
1. Choose a dig site under My journey.

2. At the named location, hold the Field Seeker and press the action button.

3. Follow the arrow along dry ground. A golden frame appears automatically when you are close.

4. Take your hoe and dig inside the frame. A flash, rising fragments and a changing counter confirm the find.

5. Restore your current project from the collected fragments under Finds.

workshop.heading.0: A story waiting to be found
workshop.text.0:
A small workshop once operated beneath the mountain. Its owner made helpers for curious travellers.

Begin with dwarven dig sites: your first find in that field will uncover a lead.
workshop.text.1:
An oiled sheet survived between layers of soil. It shows a tiny mechanical animal, with a note: 'Dig with curiosity.'

Bring your notes to the museum. Speak to Gunther at the counter, or use the button in this book while inside the museum.
workshop.text.2:
Gunther found a similar drawing in an old inventory. The machine was called a digger: it sensed traces of objects shaped by working hands.

Show Robin the blueprint. Talk to her, or open this page while standing close to her.
workshop.text.3:
Robin marked three missing components. They cost no research fragments. After speaking with her, each suitable find guarantees a missing part.

Spring: dwarven finds.
Lens: coastal finds.
Core: valley heritage finds.

Ordinary worm spots also qualify when their bonus fragment drops are enabled.
workshop.text.4:
The spring is wound, the lens is clean, and the core glows softly. Only the housing and final assembly remain.

Return to the farm or your farmhouse with 20 wood and 5 copper bars. Make room for your reward display case.
workshop.text.5:
The digger's belly reads 'Dig with curiosity.' It follows your footsteps and turns its nose toward nearby antiquities. In the evening at home, it starts to doze.

Your first case is in your backpack. Place it indoors or on the farm, and put a regular artifact on it as you would on a table.

Call or dismiss your companion here, or build additional cases.
workshop.dialogue.gunther:
Gunther carefully smooths out the blueprint.

'I've seen this drawing in an old workshop inventory. It says: a helper for those who notice the past. Robin should know how to bring it back to life.'

A copy of the record is added to your journal. Next: show the blueprint to Robin.
workshop.dialogue.robin:
Robin turns the sheet, estimating dimensions.

'What a lovely design! I can work out the housing. But you'll need a winding spring, a clear lens, and this strange core. The drawing marks three different places. Its maker must have collected parts all over the valley.'

Three notes are added to the journal: mountains, coast, and old settlements.
workshop.dialogue.complete:
First, one click. Then another. Brass paws cautiously touch the floor.

The digger sneezes a cloud of old dust and nudges your hand. Its first discovery is you.

Workshop Under the Mountain is complete! Your digger will accompany you, and your first display case is in your backpack.
weather.title: Traces of the Weather
weather.guide:
The morning after a rainy day may reveal an old encampment. After a thunderstorm, charred roots can expose an underhill mechanism.

A special site contains 3 finds and lasts {{days}} days. Your instrument prioritizes it before ordinary digs.

The first completion of each type grants a new relic. Repeats give extra fragments and a keystone.

At least {{cooldown}} days separate new sites. Unfinished sites remain until their expiry. Unclaimed rewards wait in the journal indefinitely.

shipwreck.title: Letters from the Sunken Schooner
shipwreck.discovered: Three stars on a buckle… A sunken schooner story has opened in your journal!
shipwreck.heading.1: Three stars without a return date
shipwreck.heading.6: The voice of the Three Stars
shipwreck.text.0: Restore the Sunken Schooner Buckle in the sea culture. Its mark is your first lead. If you have already restored it, the story opens automatically when you load your save, even if you donated or sold the item.
shipwreck.text.1: Three stars have emerged on the buckle. Visit the museum, open this page inside the building and study the harbour records with Gunther. You do not need to hand over the buckle.
shipwreck.text.2: Gunther found the schooner Three Stars. She disappeared off the valley's coast, yet no losses were recorded. A knot is drawn in the margin. Approach Willy and ask him about it; the button below works near the fisherman wherever he is.
shipwreck.text.3: Willy recognises his old mentor's knot, used to seal letters in bottles. Play a rainy or stormy day, then survey the western beach the following morning. The bottle can be found for three days after rain. If you miss it, another rainy day gives you a new chance. This story works even when ordinary weather expeditions are disabled.
shipwreck.text.4: A sealed bottle lay beneath the sand. The paper survived; you can reread the letter in your journal. It mentions 'quiet water beyond the old landing'. Approach Willy to understand the captain's words.
shipwreck.text.5: Willy explained that the captain meant the old landing on the western beach. Survey that shore and excavate three finds in the final cache. Take your time: there is no deadline, and you do not need to repair the tide-pool bridge.
shipwreck.text.6: A ship's bell emerged from the sand, wrapped in an old sail. A note beside it reads: 'Everyone made it ashore. May it call us home again someday.' The bell will wait in your journal until you have backpack space.
shipwreck.text.7: The Three Stars never logged her return: the sailors went home on foot, leaving the damaged ship to the sea. Her bell can sing on dry land again. Place it at home or on the farm and press the action button to restore 35 energy once per day. All copies share one charge per player; full energy preserves it. The letter remains in the journal archive.
shipwreck.dialogue.gunther: Gunther traces an old entry with his finger.^The Three Stars. Departure date, cargo… but no return entry. Yet not a single name among the lost.^See this knot in the margin? I've copied it into your journal. Ask Willy. He knows sea signs better than my dusty shelves.
shipwreck.dialogue.willy: Willy studies the sketch for a long time.^My old mentor used that knot to seal letters for the folks waiting ashore. A sturdy binding. That bottle could have spent years in the sand.^Rain washes the top layer away. Check the western beach the next morning, friend. Your instrument ought to pick it up.
shipwreck.dialogue.decode: Willy smooths out a copy of the letter.^'Quiet water'… Old sailors called the place by the western landing that. Not across the bridge. Right beside the road home.^They took the bell off before she sank. They must have reached the shore. Find that cache, friend. Give this story its voice back.
shipwreck.letter:
Dear Mara,

If this bottle reaches you before we do, don't believe the rumours about the ship. Everyone is ashore. Even our grumpy cook.

We took the bell down before the water reached the deck and hid it where the sea grows quiet beyond the old landing. Three marks in the sand will show the place.

The schooner will stay here. We will walk home. Perhaps this time I won't smell of fresh fish, though I make no promises.

Yours, Elias.
Captain of the Three Stars.

On the back, in another hand: 'Everyone made it. May it call us home again someday.'

nature.guide.snow: The first observed snowy day of each year leaves a lead for the next morning. Three finds appear in the forest, backwoods or town for {{days}} days. Installing on a snowy day also counts as the first observation.
nature.guide.season: The first day of a new season opens three beach finds for {{days}} days. The mod must observe the season change; installing on the first day does not create a retroactive event.

nature.rules: The first completion of each kind gives a unique artifact, stored in the journal until claimed. Repeat sites grant fragments, experience and a keystone. Snow and shore: +12 fragments and 45 experience; meteor: +18 and 75. All three kinds can coexist. Finds avoid water, crops and buildings. The hourglass can extend a site once.

residents.goal.evelyn: The swallow brooch reminds Evelyn of a springtime promise. Her lead follows forest paths to an old garden's traces.

residents.dialogue.penny.start: May I see your notes? Runes aren't my specialty... but I recognise these repetitions. A pupil tries to write a symbol, gets frustrated, and rubs everything out.#$b#I might skip the bit about the teacher's moustache when reading to the children. Though Vincent would probably love it.#$b#Between the lines there's a path and two flat stones. It looks like the old town paths. Try your instrument there. Perhaps the rest of the lesson survived?
residents.dialogue.penny.share: The first tablet has the same symbol carved seven times. The second says... 'Once more. Better already.' So the teacher was patient after all.#$b#I'll keep a copy for our lessons. Sometimes a child needs to see that even an ancient teacher allowed mistakes.#$b#Take this seal. We can put it beside little discoveries. For paying attention, rather than getting the answer right.
residents.note.penny: Two practice tablets. Seven uneven symbols cover the first; the teacher wrote 'Once more. Better already.' on the second. A small moustache in the margin has been carefully framed.
residents.dialogue.evelyn.start: Oh, that little swallow... People gave those brooches with a promise to return in spring. I remember waiting for the birds by the road with my friend.#$b#We had a tiny garden beyond the forest path. We hid tin notes there about what we'd plant next year, like very grown-up gardeners.#$b#Perhaps the soil kept one. Try your instrument along the forest paths. Take your time. A good story, like a garden, knows how to wait.
residents.dialogue.evelyn.share: 'We'll plant more in spring. Even if they don't all grow.' My goodness... I'd forgotten those words, yet I kept living by them.#$b#There weren't any rare flowers. Just two girls, a handful of seeds and a very serious promise to meet again in spring. It was enough.#$b#I put a petal from my garden today in this locket. Take it. When you're tired, remember: you can start a new garden at any age.
residents.note.evelyn: Two tin covers show a child's drawing of a swallow and a garden. A paper inside reads: 'We'll plant more in spring. Even if they don't all grow.' The names faded; the promise survived.
residents.dialogue.willy.start: A little fish whistle? Ha! A proper shore thing. You'd use it to call a boat when your voice was lost in the wind, though never in a storm.#$b#Two short notes, one long. My father answered that way when I waited for his catch. I always whistled too early, then went red as a lobster.#$b#They left signal notes near the old paths on the western beach. Try your instrument there. You won't need the bridge to the pools.
residents.dialogue.willy.share: There's the note. 'Don't whistle until you see the sail.' Good advice... wish someone had told me.#$b#The other side says: 'If you're waiting, let them know you're here.' That one's more important. Someone in a boat is glad to hear a familiar sound too.#$b#I cleaned an old brass whistle for you. Two short notes, one long. May it guide you to the things waiting in the soil.
residents.note.willy: Pieces of a shore signal guide show a boat and a fish. One side reads 'Don't whistle until you see the sail.' The other: 'If you're waiting, let them know you're here.' Nothing about treasure; only coming home.

exp.intro.river: After the primer story, Penny returned to the school's field notes. Between the pages lay a strip marked with water levels. The resonant lens revealed float marks, but its label had faded. Penny does not want another story of the valley's caretakers to disappear.
exp.dialogue.river.1: Penny: I meant to prepare a lesson about old bridges, but found somebody's watch roster. Beside each name is a line, sometimes two, and a note: 'Where the great river bends around the woodland path.' I think people took turns watching the water. Will you help find what they used? Your lens showed that the marks were worn into the wood by a moving float.
exp.dialogue.river.4: Maru: This axle has no circular wear. It did not turn a mill; its lever rocked up and down. The scale narrows near the top, where every mark matters. The other half of the note says: 'Checked at the source below the mountain slopes.' I'd look where the water is still cold and fast. Let's find the remaining parts, then hold a proper field inspection.
exp.dialogue.river.10: Penny: So it was neither a clock nor a mill, but a river watch. One person noticed the rising water; another warned the people crossing the bridge. The roster has no grand names, only neighbours. Maru will make us a safe model, and I'll label it: 'The valley depended on people who stopped to care.' Thank you for giving their care a name again.
exp.clue.river.1: 'The great river bends around the woodland path. The watcher looks at water, not a clock.' A wide bend is drawn beside the note; no such bridge can be seen from the quiet path behind the farm.
exp.clue.river.2: The axle rocked rather than spun. 'Checked at the source below the mountain slopes.' Look upstream, where the river comes from the mountains.
exp.evidence.river.1: Recovered: an unevenly divided scale and a narrow axle. The axle has two wear lines, rather than a full circle. Through the lens you can see river deposits.
exp.evidence.river.2: All four parts: scale, axle, light float and supporting frame. The float changes height, the axle transfers movement and the scale makes a dangerous rise in water visible.
exp.meeting.river.0: Penny: I checked the names. The watch passed from house to house; nobody stood by the river alone all night. This instrument was part of a shared promise to care for neighbours.
exp.meeting.river.1: Maru: Put the scale to the float's right, the frame below the float and the axle below the scale. That gives the lever room to move. The water marks line up across the parts.
exp.meeting.river.2: Penny: The highest line in the note is marked 'call'. Not 'harvest' or 'begin the shift', just 'call'. They had time to warn the people still at the bridge.
exp.meeting.river.3: Which observation explains the axle, the float and the school note together?
exp.assembly-guide.river: Float left of scale. Frame below float; axle below scale. Change the assembly freely.
exp.intro.tide: After the harbour story, Willy noticed four loops on the old buckle. Leo had seen the same pattern in island weaving. Willy suggests tracing the object between two shores. It may remember a return journey, rather than buried treasure.
exp.dialogue.tide.1: Willy: Harbours love grand tales of distant voyages. I keep thinking about people who returned in little boats without a compass. The buckle has four loops, like stops along a cord. An old note says: 'Begin where the valley boats rest on sand; stay on this side of the tide-pool bridge.' Let's start at the familiar shore. We won't need the bridge.
exp.dialogue.tide.4: Leo: I know those knots. You can read them with your fingers while watching the waves. A shell means sea; a stone means trees and land. But the last knot does not lead to a tree home. It says: 'From here, the boat will take you home.' Search the island shore where visitors first arrive and the return boat waits. Then we'll look together: each of us knows half the journey.
exp.dialogue.tide.10: Willy: A reminder of the way home... Not an order about where to go, but a way to remember what waits there. Leo says another knot was tied after every safe return. I thought I knew every useful sailing instrument. Sometimes the most important one serves the person, rather than the boat. Let's make a light mobile, bringing shell, stone and thread together again. The old find will remain our shared story.
exp.clue.tide.1: 'The valley boats rest on sand; stay on this side of the tide-pool bridge.' Sand is caught in the cord's first loop. No marks lie beyond the bridge.
exp.clue.tide.2: Knots can be read by touch, and the shell means sea. The last loop marks a return rather than the start of a forest trail: 'Here the island welcomes visitors; here the boat waits to take them home.' Salt remains on the bead.
exp.evidence.tide.1: Recovered: a wooden frame and a drilled shell. There is no magnetic needle, degree scale or gearing. Soft cord marks remain inside the hole.
exp.evidence.tide.2: Four parts: frame, shell, knotted cord and stone bead. The knots follow a stable sequence. The object distinguishes shore, forest and return; it does not measure a boat's speed.
exp.meeting.tide.0: Willy: This object has no north. I turned the frame, and the knots kept their meaning. We were wrong to look for an ordinary compass.
exp.meeting.tide.1: Leo: Shell at the upper left, stone at the right. Frame below the shell, cord below the stone. First remember the sea, then land, then home. A knot keeps the sequence, rather than the distance.
exp.meeting.tide.2: Willy: Leo and I know different shores, yet we can read one journey. Perhaps that is what this simple object was for: letting one person's memory help another return.
exp.meeting.tide.3: Which conclusion fits every part and both accounts?

artifact.harvest_seal.lore: Touching soil with this seal reveals long-forgotten field boundaries, leading to traces of the valley's early settlements.
artifact.memory_musicbox.name: Music Box of Kind Memories
artifact.memory_musicbox.description: Right-click: restore 40 health. Once per day.
artifact.memory_musicbox.lore: The melody changes a little each time. It sounds like something a loved one once hummed while rain tapped at the window.
artifact.forest_heart.name: Heart of the First Forest
artifact.forest_heart.description: An ancient glowing relic. Place it in your home or on the farm.
artifact.forest_heart.lore: An amber droplet holds a leaf from a tree older than the first house in the valley. Even in winter, its light feels like summer.
artifact.brass_gear.name: Ancient Lift Gear
artifact.brass_gear.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.brass_gear.lore: A tiny rune marks every tooth. Dwarven mechanics seem to have numbered their parts to repair machines in total darkness.
artifact.rune_tablet.name: Apprentice Runecarver's Tablet
artifact.rune_tablet.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.rune_tablet.lore: The final line reads 'I will stop drawing a moustache on my teacher.' The earlier lines were carefully scraped away.
artifact.miner_goblet.name: Underhill Master's Goblet
artifact.miner_goblet.description: A table ornament and a research archive exhibit.
artifact.miner_goblet.lore: Heavy, yet perfectly balanced. Its rim reads: 'Good work begins after a good lunch.'
artifact.dwarf_thermos.name: Dwarven Thermos
artifact.dwarf_thermos.description: Right-click: receive a Triple Shot Espresso. Once per day.
artifact.dwarf_thermos.lore: The lid has three settings: 'hot', 'very hot', and 'break time is over'. Fortunately, the last setting is stuck.
artifact.resonant_lens.name: Resonant Lens
artifact.resonant_lens.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal an exact find. Once per day.
artifact.resonant_lens.lore: Through the glass, faint echoes of hammer strikes are visible. The lens reveals places once shaped by working hands.
artifact.clockwork_mole.name: Clockwork Digger
artifact.clockwork_mole.description: Right-click at a dig site: pinpoint a find. Once per day.
artifact.clockwork_mole.lore: This tiny brass animal stubbornly turns its nose toward buried antiquities. Its belly is engraved: 'Dig with curiosity.'
artifact.mountain_heart.name: Memory of the Deep Mountain
artifact.mountain_heart.description: Right-click: gain 8 dwarven fragments. Once per day.
artifact.mountain_heart.lore: This crystal remembers the shape of objects once placed beside it. Bridges and stairways of an underground city flicker in its depths.
artifact.clay_whistle.name: Sailor's Clay Whistle
artifact.clay_whistle.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.clay_whistle.lore: Shaped like a fish, perhaps a gift to a child before a long voyage. Fine white sand fills the opening.
artifact.sailor_buckle.name: Sunken Schooner Buckle
artifact.sailor_buckle.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.sailor_buckle.lore: Beneath the salt is an image of three stars. Gunther found a ship of the same name in the harbour records, without a return date.
artifact.shell_comb.name: Mother-of-Pearl Comb
artifact.shell_comb.description: A table ornament and a research archive exhibit.
artifact.shell_comb.lore: Every tooth follows the shell's curve. At dusk, the comb casts reflections resembling distant sails.
artifact.tide_compass.name: Tide Compass
artifact.tide_compass.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal an exact find. Once per day.
artifact.tide_compass.lore: The needle knows nothing of north. It seeks things someone once missed dearly. Sailors considered that more useful.
artifact.pearl_casket.name: Salt-Pearl Casket
artifact.pearl_casket.description: Right-click: receive 3 clams. Once per day.
artifact.pearl_casket.lore: A tiny wave can be heard inside. Every morning, gifts from a distant shore appear despite the lid being closed all night.
artifact.moon_shell.name: Moon-Tide Shell
artifact.moon_shell.description: Right-click: restore 60 energy. Once per day.
artifact.moon_shell.lore: Inside is the sea from no known map. Listening makes your breathing steady and lets weariness drift away.
artifact.abyss_beacon.name: Beacon of Forgotten Depths
artifact.abyss_beacon.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal an exact find. Once per day.
artifact.abyss_beacon.lore: This light guided travellers where the sun never shone. Its base bears a map of a coastline long since claimed by the sea.
artifact.rain_pitcher.name: Pitcher of the First Rain
artifact.rain_pitcher.description: Right-click: water up to 9 tilled tiles in front of you. Once per day; no charge is spent without dry soil.
artifact.rain_pitcher.lore: A tiny cloud was painted beneath the forest silt. Rain gathers in the pitcher every morning, though nobody has filled it for years.
artifact.storm_fork.name: Storm Tuning Fork
artifact.storm_fork.description: Right-click: reveal all dig-site finds within 8 tiles for 30 seconds. Once per day; hoe the highlighted tiles.
artifact.storm_fork.lore: Lightning exposed this instrument beneath charred roots. A quiet chord trembles between its prongs; underhill makers heard forgotten objects answer it.
artifact.past_lens.name: Lens of the Past
artifact.past_lens.description: Right-click: reveal a walkable trail of footprints to the nearest find and its old inscription for 30 seconds. Once a day; no trail preserves the charge.
artifact.past_lens.lore: The marks in its glass are tiny paths, not scratches. A dwarven maker engraved the rim: 'Things remember the way home, even when people forget.'
artifact.garden_flute.name: Forgotten Orchard Flute
artifact.garden_flute.description: Right-click near a fruit tree: grow one extra fruit, once every 7 game days. Requires a healthy mature tree in season, holding fewer than three fruits, within 5 tiles. Greenhouse season rules apply.
artifact.garden_flute.lore: A gardener played this flute while waiting for letters from distant lands. The trees grew used to her melody and still answer with a quiet rustle.
artifact.keeper_hourglass.name: Keeper's Hourglass
artifact.keeper_hourglass.description: Right-click at a dig location: report remaining finds and extend the nearest eligible site by one day. Once a day, once per site. Story caches cannot be extended.
artifact.keeper_hourglass.lore: The upper bulb never empties while someone carefully sorts their pottery shards. The keeper seems to have valued unfinished stories above timetables.
artifact.pocket_observatory.name: Pocket Observatory
artifact.pocket_observatory.description: Right-click outdoors after 8pm: forecast and open a two-find star expedition the next morning. Once a day; only one pending or active star expedition. Lasts 3 days from its first morning.
artifact.pocket_observatory.lore: Sailors carried it instead of heavy charts. Its needles point not north, but where tomorrow's light will first touch something long forgotten.
artifact.frozen_leaf.name: Sleeping Leaf Imprint
artifact.frozen_leaf.description: A rare find after the first snow. A golden leaf rests inside thin ice. Display it, donate it to Gunther's archive, or sell it.
artifact.frozen_leaf.lore: Someone scratched 'Until spring' on the back. They wanted to preserve their garden's last leaf, and winter kept the promise for them.
artifact.tide_calendar.name: Calendar of Four Tides
artifact.tide_calendar.description: A rare coastal find at the turn of a season. Four colored inlays mark the year's cycle. Display it, donate it to Gunther's archive, or sell it.
artifact.tide_calendar.lore: Sailors marked the first warm wind, the longest day, red leaves and still water before snow. This calendar, rather than the stars, told them when to come home.
artifact.star_glass.name: Star Glass
artifact.star_glass.description: An epic find in the soil beside a new meteorite on the farm. A cold light glimmers in dark glass. Display it, donate it to Gunther's archive, or sell it.
artifact.star_glass.lore: Dwarven makers called such shards 'windows without walls'. Gaze into its depths and a distant light seems to draw slowly closer.
artifact.reader_seal.name: Careful Reader's Seal
artifact.reader_seal.description: Right-click: +8 dwarven fragments once a day. A keepsake from Penny's story. All copies share one charge per player.
artifact.reader_seal.lore: Penny wrote 'try again' beside the dwarven mark. It now appears on every page that used to say 'wrong'.
artifact.garden_locket.name: First Garden Locket
artifact.garden_locket.description: Right-click: restore up to 60 energy once a day. A keepsake from Evelyn's story. Full energy preserves the charge.
artifact.garden_locket.lore: A pressed petal rests behind the glass. Evelyn says flowers grow better when you promise someone you'll show them in spring.
artifact.harbor_whistle.name: Quiet Harbour Whistle
artifact.harbor_whistle.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal the nearest find once a day. A keepsake from Willy's story. No available find preserves the charge.
artifact.harbor_whistle.lore: Two short notes, one long. Willy says the signal means 'I'm here', which is sometimes all someone waiting ashore needs to hear.
artifact.caravan_token.name: Quiet Caravan Token
artifact.caravan_token.description: A copper token marked with a well. Display it or donate it to the museum archive.
artifact.caravan_token.lore: One side records the travellers; the other records the cups. The counts match. This caravan counted the people who had to reach the next well, rather than its cargo.
artifact.sun_clay_lamp.name: Sandside Rest Lamp
artifact.sun_clay_lamp.description: A small clay lamp with a broad spout. A collectible for your display case.
artifact.sun_clay_lamp.lore: Only one side is blackened. The lamp stood by a tent entrance, sheltered from the wind. Its maker's thumbprint remains underneath.
artifact.glass_route_bead.name: Long Road Glass Bead
artifact.glass_route_bead.description: Milky glass crossed by a turquoise vein. Part of the sand-road collection.
artifact.glass_route_bead.lore: Travellers moved these beads along a cord after each crossing. Turquoise meant water. Even an exhausted traveller could read this little map by touch.
artifact.sun_dial.name: Wayfarer's Sun Dial
artifact.sun_dial.description: Right-click outdoors before 6pm: +1 speed for 90 seconds. Once daily; unsuitable conditions preserve the charge.
artifact.sun_dial.lore: The tiny dial measured the time until the next shade cast by a rock or tree. A caravan keeper inscribed it: 'Care for your feet, and the road will care for you.'
artifact.oasis_vial.name: Last Oasis Vial
artifact.oasis_vial.description: Right-click: restore up to 60 energy and 25 health. Once daily. Full energy and health preserve the charge.
artifact.oasis_vial.lore: A cold droplet always trembles inside. Two hands are carved into its stopper, one giving water and one receiving it. The vial was passed to the last person in the line.
artifact.island_spindle.name: Shore Weaver's Spindle
artifact.island_spindle.description: A stone spindle weight retaining traces of plant fibres. Display it or donate it to the archive.
artifact.island_spindle.lore: Its pattern repeats after seven notches. Threads were counted by the days between high tides, and finished cloth was dried well above the sand.
artifact.obsidian_scale.name: Obsidian Scale
artifact.obsidian_scale.description: A thin piece of volcanic glass pierced with a careful hole. A collectible find.
artifact.obsidian_scale.lore: It bears no traces of weapon use. Hung above a hearth, the black glass caught the light and warned when the flames grew too strong.
artifact.woven_tide_band.name: Seven Tides Bracelet
artifact.woven_tide_band.description: Woven fibres with a tiny shell clasp. Part of the island-shore collection.
artifact.woven_tide_band.lore: One knot has been undone. A fisher returned home early and slipped the final day's wait from their wrist. The clasp preserves the name of someone who waited.
artifact.turtle_charm.name: Keeper's Stone Turtle
artifact.turtle_charm.description: Right-click: +3 defence and +64 pixels of item attraction for 90 seconds. Once daily.
artifact.turtle_charm.lore: Tiny houses cover its shell. The shore keeper carried it in a pocket and said that a safe shelter begins with caring for those nearby.
artifact.tide_conch.name: Returning Tide Conch
artifact.tide_conch.description: Right-click at a dig location: reveal up to two accessible, unmarked finds. Once daily. No suitable targets preserves the charge.
artifact.tide_conch.lore: Listen closely and two short replies sound within it. Shore gatherers used them to mark a safe route before the water hid their tracks again.
opening.title: Tea in a New Home
opening.gunther-start: An old museum notebook mentions pottery fragments in the countryside. I marked a site on My Journey in your journal. Perhaps we can learn what they belonged to.^Here are your journal and field surveyor. Bring an ordinary hoe. Use the surveyor at the site, then dig inside the golden outline when it appears.^Take your time: this first site will stay. Once you have restored an object, come back and we will see what story it kept.
opening.summary.2:
Find the potsherds.
Restore the cup.
The site has no deadline.
opening.text.2:
A museum notebook contains a note about pottery fragments in the countryside. Gunther marked a place to begin looking in your journal.

"Large stories sometimes begin with ordinary dishes. Try piecing together one object first. Then we will have something to discuss."

My Journey lists the location. Use the surveyor to find the fragments and your hoe to unearth them.
opening.text.fragments:
Traces of glaze remain on the first sherds. The curved rim suggests a small cup. Its story is still unknown: the pieces need to be joined.

The journal stores your fragments without using backpack space. The project page shows how many you have collected. Once you have enough, restore the cup and return to Gunther.

The remaining sherds will stay at the site if you decide to continue another day.
opening.summary.3:
The cup is restored.
Your notes are ready.
Visit Gunther at the museum.
opening.text.3:
The pieces form a plain clay cup. Scratched into its base are the words: "In a new place, tea still smells like home."

A small maker's mark remains on the handle. You copied both the inscription and the mark into your journal to show Gunther.

Visit him at the museum. Talk at his counter or open this entry and use its conversation button. The cup stays yours; your notes are enough even if the object is already on display at home.
opening.summary.4:
The cup's story is recorded.
Next clue: mountain workshops.
opening.conversation: "In a new place, tea still smells like home"… A few words from someone who missed home, rather than a record of a great event. We do not know their name yet. The clay and glaze suggest the first settlements, before the railway.^I recognize the mark in your sketch. Similar stamps appear on objects from the old mountain workshops. The cup was used here, but may have travelled from the mountains. I marked that field of research in your journal.^There is our first story: someone came to the valley and brought a little of their old home with them. You may keep the cup. Thank you for returning with your notes; now we have another clue to follow.
opening.goal.dig:
Gunther found a note about pottery fragments in a museum notebook and marked the site: {{location}}. Finds remaining: {{count}}.

Hold the surveyor, follow it to the golden outline and dig with your hoe. Fragments stay in your journal. This first dig has no deadline.
opening.goal.restore:
You have enough sherds to piece together the cup. Open "{{artifact}}" in Finds and restore it for {{cost}} fragments. The finished object needs a free inventory slot.

Then return to Gunther: he promised to help read its story.
opening.goal.talk:
The cup is restored, and its inscription and maker's mark are copied in your journal. Return to Gunther at the museum and discuss the find.

Talk at his counter or open this entry and use its conversation button while inside the museum. You do not need to donate the cup or carry it with you.
opening.goal.wait: Gunther marked your first dig, but no free ground could be found there yet. The note is saved. The site will appear when a reachable spot is available; no deadline is running.
opening.next-search: Begin at the site Gunther marked on My Journey. Collect the sherds, restore the cup and return to the museum with your notes. There is no need to hurry.
learn.tip.homecoming: Discuss your notes about the cup with Gunther at the museum.
learn.text.homecoming:
Your first cup is restored. You copied its inscription and maker's mark into the journal. Return to the museum and talk to Gunther at his counter.

You can also open Research → Tea in a New Home and use the conversation button while inside the museum. The cup is not consumed and you do not need to carry it.

Gunther will help finish your first story and explain the next clue. The conversation stays in the entry for rereading.
routes.title: Where Finds Lead
routes.source: This clue began with a restored find: "{{artifact}}".
routes.clue.sea:
The cleaned gear belonged to a lifting machine. But what did it lift: ore in a mine or cargo beside the water?

You sketched the wheel and its hub. Willy knows the old wharves and may recognize the mechanism from your drawing.
routes.clue.calico:
Fine white sand remained inside the clay whistle. This coastal find may have travelled far before being left on the shore.

Gunther collects records of the valley's roads and trade. Now that the Calico bus is running, you can compare the coastal finds with his overland maps.
routes.clue.island:
Three stars appeared beneath the salt on the buckle. The sign is copied in your journal, but does not explain where the ship sailed.

Willy keeps old coastal records. With the island boat available, you can ask about the other side of the strait before beginning fieldwork there.
routes.instructions.sea: Speak to Willy beside him, or open this entry and use its conversation button. He must be nearby, awake and available to talk. The gear can stay at home: your sketch is enough.
routes.instructions.calico: Visit Gunther at the museum. Talk at his counter or open this entry and use its conversation button while inside. The whistle is not consumed; your notes are enough.
routes.instructions.island: Find Willy and show him your notes through a normal conversation or this page's button. He must be nearby, awake and available to talk. You do not need to carry the buckle.
routes.conversation.sea: Yes, I recognize that shape in your drawing. Wheels like these went into hand-operated hoists: they lifted crates from boats at the old wharf. I cannot say this exact gear stood there, but it is worth comparing.^A road connected the mountain workshops with life on the shore. Traces of the old wharves remain on the beach. Mark the coast in your journal and try your familiar surveyor there.^You will not need another tool. Keep sea fragments separately: objects weathered by salt and water need their own pieces. Let us see what the shore has kept.
routes.conversation.calico: A few grains of sand cannot tell us where an object came from. But your whistle brings a useful thought: the shore was the end of a road. The museum inventory includes a map of caravan stops between the valley and Calico.^It marks wells and resting places. With the bus running again, you can compare the map with the land. I added the sandy route to your field notes; the first digs will be in the desert.^Use the same surveyor and hoe. We will keep Calico fragments separately. Now the road can have a story of its own, beyond its marks on a map.
routes.conversation.island: Three stars… That sign appears beside an entry for a visit to the island's southern shore in the old coastal records. It does not settle the schooner's story, but gives us a place to compare with the find.^With the boat running, begin on the southern shore or in the eastern jungle. Look for traces of craft and daily life there. You do not need the passage to the western farm.^I marked the island field in your journal. You already know how to use the surveyor near water. Keep island fragments separately and let the objects tell us who lived across the strait.
routes.goal.sea:
After restoring "{{artifact}}", you sketched the lifting mechanism. Find Willy: he can compare it with old wharf equipment.

Talk beside him or open Research → Where Finds Lead. Your drawing is enough; the item is not consumed. This clue has no deadline.
routes.goal.calico:
Sand remained inside "{{artifact}}". The bus is available, and Gunther keeps records of caravan roads. Discuss the connection between the coast and overland travel.

Talk at his museum counter or open Where Finds Lead. Your journal is enough, and the clue has no deadline.
routes.goal.island:
The find "{{artifact}}" carries three stars. The island boat is available; Willy can compare the sign with his coastal records.

Talk beside him or open Where Finds Lead. You do not need to carry the buckle. This clue has no deadline.
routes.empty: New routes begin with recovered objects and conversations. An entry will appear when there is something to compare.
routes.next-mountain: Gunther recognized the first cup's mark and pointed you toward the mountain workshops. Continue their research: restored mechanisms may show which other places they were connected to.
routes.wait.calico: The road to Calico is available. Keep researching familiar fields: a real find will reveal a connection with the caravan route.
routes.wait.island: The island boat is available. Keep studying coastal objects so Willy can compare your next clue with his records.
learn.title.routes: From a find to a new path
learn.tip.routes: Open Research → Where Finds Lead for the source and next conversation.
learn.text.routes:
A restored object may suggest where to search next. Where Finds Lead records which find gave you a clue and who can help explain it.

Discuss the entry with the named resident. The conversation opens ordinary fieldwork in the new region and stays in your journal. The object is not consumed: your notes are enough. Clues have no deadline.

One new conversation is shown at a time. Recorded stories stay beside it; future routes and rewards are not listed in advance.
